name: Nandrolone
lead: Nandrolone, also called 19-nortestosterone, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from testosterone by removal of one methyl group, and it is the parent compound of the 19-nor AAS subclass.[1] It is usually given as an injectable ester, most often nandrolone decanoate (brand name Deca-Durabolin).[1]

Medically it has been used for catabolic and wasting conditions such as anaemia of chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis, and tissue loss in HIV and burn patients.[1] Outside medicine it is used by bodybuilders and other athletes for muscle size, strength and recovery, usually at higher doses than therapeutic ones.[1][2] A systematic review of illicit nandrolone decanoate use describes it as a widespread class of drugs among adolescents and bodybuilders.[2]

Clinical trials in patients have examined lean mass, bone and blood outcomes, but no controlled trial in healthy people was found among the sources reviewed. In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a muscle drug said to be easier on hair and skin than testosterone, and as a possible aid to bone growth.
infobox: US Schedule III; prohibited in sport

paras: Nandrolone esters have been indicated for anaemia associated with chronic kidney disease, postmenopausal osteoporosis, and wasting in HIV/AIDS or burns, where they stimulate red blood cell production and help preserve lean mass.[1] Medical doses are described as far lower than illicit ones.[1]

Non-medical users take nandrolone for muscle growth, strength and joint or recovery benefits within bodybuilding, often combined with testosterone.[1][2] On looksmax.org, users discuss deca as a muscle compound said not to cause hair loss, and some argue it may support bone density or growth.[3][4]

Nandrolone acts as an agonist of the androgen receptor, with an anabolic-to-androgenic ratio in rodent assays of about 11 to 1 compared with 1 to 1 for testosterone.[1] Unlike testosterone, it is converted by 5-alpha-reductase to 5-alpha-dihydronandrolone, a weaker androgen, which is the basis for forum claims that it is 'hair safe'.[1][3] It also has progestogenic activity.[1]

It is made semi-synthetically from estrone by Birch reduction, a route first described in 1953.[1] Esterification at the 17-beta hydroxyl creates oil-soluble depots such as the decanoate for intramuscular injection.[1]

Trials have tested nandrolone decanoate in patients, not in healthy lifters. A randomised trial studied it in burned patients, with the authors suggesting a possible new indication after its recall;[5] a randomised trial in men with osteoporosis examined bone outcomes;[6] and a phase 1/2 study of 20 people with telomere-related bone marrow failure and lung disease has been completed,[7] with an editorial discussing nandrolone as a possible option for telomeropathies.[8] Registered studies also covered HIV-associated weight loss in women,[9] cancer cachexia,[10] and muscle loss with leucine.[11]

A forum poster cites a study in dialysis patients reporting that 6 months of weekly nandrolone raised lean body mass, offered as evidence for the compound.[3] No trial of nandrolone for cosmetic or bodybuilding purposes in healthy people appears in the sources reviewed.

A 2020 systematic review of 148 papers on nandrolone decanoate abuse and adverse effects summarised the most frequent effects in abusers, with reproductive and other organ systems affected.[2] A separate review of sudden cardiac death in AAS users examined cardiac mechanisms in 33 reported cases across the drug class.[12] Users on looksmax.org note that both testosterone and deca suppress natural testosterone production, and one thread is titled as a complaint that deca caused insulin resistance.[13][14]

Nandrolone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States and is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency; its metabolites are monitored in urine, although low endogenous production complicates threshold testing.[1] T Nation posters note that prescriptions for supraphysiological doses of testosterone, nandrolone and related drugs are a legal grey area.[15]

timeline.event: Birch reduction route to the 19-nor steroid skeleton first described.[1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, deca is promoted by some as a muscle, skin and bone drug and dismissed by others as unnecessary and suppressive.[3][4][13]

claims.claim: Deca is 'hair safe' because it converts to a weak androgen.
claims.believers: A thread author says deca does not convert to DHT but to DHN, so hair loss risk is 'extremely minimal'.[3]
claims.experts: The pharmacology of 5-alpha reduction to a weaker androgen is described in encyclopedic sources,[1] but no trial in this review tested hair outcomes.

claims.claim: Deca builds a lot of muscle, as shown by trials.
claims.believers: The same author cites a 6-month dialysis trial reporting lean mass gains of about 4.5 kg.[3]
claims.experts: Randomised trials in patients with wasting and burns exist,[5] but results from sick patients do not directly test use in healthy people.

claims.believers: A poster argued nandrolone decanoate shifts bone remodelling toward formation and suppresses resorption more than other AAS.[4]
claims.experts: A randomised trial studied nandrolone for osteoporosis in men.[6] No studies were found showing it increases adult height, and other forum users objected to the theory in the thread.[4]

claims.claim: Some users consider Deca unnecessary alongside testosterone and HGH.
claims.believers: A reply in one thread calls deca 'worthless' and notes both deca and test suppress natural production.[13]
claims.experts: Reviews report suppression of reproductive function with AAS abuse.[2]

claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread title states this as a user finding.[14]
claims.experts: No study in this review addressed insulin resistance with nandrolone.

card.summary: A prescription-origin injectable steroid used for muscle; trials show lean-mass effects in sick patients, but none in healthy lifters.
card.note: Controlled substance and banned in sport; suppresses natural testosterone production; height claims untested.

quick.overview:
Nandrolone is an injectable anabolic steroid, best known as nandrolone decanoate (Deca-Durabolin). It has been prescribed for wasting, anaemia and osteoporosis, and is used by bodybuilders for muscle gain.

Trials in patients show effects on lean mass and related outcomes. No controlled trials in healthy people for appearance were found. Looksmaxxing posts promote it as hair-friendly and as a possible bone aid; the latter is untested.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen receptor and, unlike testosterone, is converted to a weaker androgen (DHN) rather than DHT. It also has progestogenic activity.
quick.risks: Reviews of illicit use report adverse effects across several organ systems, and cardiac deaths have been reported in AAS users generally. It suppresses natural testosterone production, is a US Schedule III drug, and is prohibited in sport.
